---
title: "RiparianBuffers"
output: html_document

# Purpose

This module creates `sim$Riparian$riparianFraction`, an exact projected
vector-intersection coverage raster on the supplied `PlanningGrid`. It is a
separate result from `sim$Riparian` and never changes the original module.

# Meaning of the fraction

> The output measures combined lake-and-riparian-buffer coverage, not riparian
> land alone. Mapped lake water surfaces are included along with policy-width
> buffers on surrounding land. A planning cell entirely inside a mapped lake
> and the study area has `riparianFraction = 1`. Lake water overlapped by stream
> or lake buffers is counted once, not added repeatedly. The denominator is the
> full planning-cell area, including water. Cells entirely outside the study
> area are `NA`. These values are a hydrological influence/coverage signal, not
> a classification of harvestable land.

The engine unions policy buffer polygons and lake interiors before intersecting
them with cells. Thus 10 ha buffered land plus 5 ha lake water in a 100 ha cell
is $0.15$, not a land-normalized fraction. Stream centrelines provide buffers
but not explicit river-water polygons. The lake polygon is the only water
surface included directly.

```text
stream ───── buffer ────────┐
                            ├─ union once ── cell intersection
mapped lake interior ───────┘
```

# Policy and geometry

Buffers use the receiving (destination) jurisdiction's width, including for a
feature on the other side of a boundary, and are then clipped to that receiving
jurisdiction. Lake interiors are independent of policy and jurisdiction
coverage. `ORD_STRA >= 4` is a large stream and `Lake_area >= 1` km² is a large
lake. The bundled six-province/default table is an analytical assumption, not
legal advice. Unmatched jurisdictions are recorded as default-policy fallback.

All widths and areas are planar in the projected metre CRS of `PlanningGrid`.
“Exact” denotes polygon--cell intersection within floating-point tolerance,
not a perfect curve, geodesic area, or a completeness claim about hydrology.

Cell coverage is calculated with `exactextractr`, avoiding explicit GEOS
intersections for every cell. Runtime packages are `SpaDES.core`, `terra`, `sf`,
and `exactextractr`. The absolute numerical acceptance tolerance is 1e-6 in
coverage fraction (1 m² per 1000 m cell), recorded as `coverageTolerance`.

# Inputs and outputs

`studyArea` is required. `PlanningGrid` is a common, read-only input; absent a
supplied/upstream grid, standalone preparation creates a 240 m fallback. The
optional unsuffixed inputs are `Jurisdiction`, `riparianBufferPolicy`,
`Hydrology_streams`, and `Hydrology_lakes`. Missing streams and lakes are
obtained independently from HydroRIVERS North America and HydroLAKES global.
Internet and substantial cache storage are required for that route.

The output list includes policy, source/projection metadata, geometry-repair
and fallback diagnostics, and `lakeInteriorsExcluded = FALSE`. It intentionally
has no original-module `raster_m` field.

# Vector export

`exportVectorBuffer = TRUE` by default writes the final unioned
lake-and-buffer numerator as `riparian_buffers.gpkg` next to the GeoTIFF.
`FALSE` writes the identical raster but no vector file. The GeoPackage is a
single file with one layer, `riparian_buffers`, and has no practical size limit
(a Shapefile would stop at 2 GiB). Its short `tile_id` field marks tile-core
pieces. Tile seams can remain in the vector layer, are not ecological
boundaries, and do not duplicate coverage.

# Minimal supplied-input run

```{r, eval=FALSE}
sim <- SpaDES.core::simInit(
  times = list(start = 1, end = 1), modules = "RiparianBuffers",
  objects = list(studyArea = studyArea, PlanningGrid = PlanningGrid,
                 Jurisdiction = Jurisdiction,
                 Hydrology_streams = Hydrology_streams,
                 Hydrology_lakes = Hydrology_lakes),
  params = list(RiparianBuffers = list(
    tileCells = 128L, exportVectorBuffer = TRUE)))
sim <- SpaDES.core::spades(sim)
fraction <- sim$Riparian$riparianFraction
```

For a joint run, explicitly supply one shared `PlanningGrid` and select either
`Riparian$riparianFraction` or `Riparian$riparianFraction` downstream.
Landbase's existing load order and input target the original result; adopting
the new result requires separate explicit integration work.
